title: Unique normalization of coherent coefficient comparisons
statement: Let B be a preorder with least element b0, P a pseudofunctor from B to categories, and J_b functors to a category A. Suppose each arrow admits a comparison J_b isomorphic to P(f) followed by J_c, and restriction from b0 is bijective on natural endomorphisms of every J_b. There is a unique coherent comparison family whose restriction is the quotient of the prescribed comparisons from b0, with the actual composition constraint of P. It constructs a functor on the Grothendieck category, with its specified restrictions. A family of natural isomorphisms respecting the comparisons from b0 respects all normalized comparisons and induces a natural isomorphism of the Grothendieck functors. Fixed category-value transports preserve such squares.

source.place: Weil II (1.1.1) b)-d), pp.146-147; explicit part of the fibre transport argument

proof.text: Divide the desired transition by any supplied comparison to get an endomorphism after restriction from b0. Lift it and its inverse using surjectivity, and use injectivity to prove the inverse laws. Injectivity on isomorphisms gives uniqueness.

After restriction, the identity and composition laws are the triangle and pentagon identities of P. This proves coherence, hence functoriality on coefficient pairs. On the inclusion of one fibre category, the identity comparison cancels the inclusion identity constraint.

Whisker the desired path square from b0. Substitute the two normalization formulas, cancel adjacent inverse comparisons, and use naturality of the path with the pseudofunctor composition constraint. Injectivity gives the square before restriction. Componentwise naturality gives the Grothendieck path. Whiskering and naturality of the fixed cancellation comparison give the category-transport square.

proof_origin.place: Weil II (1.1.1) b)-d); complete Lean construction for lem-wf-fibre-functor-basepoint-transport

theorem Pseudofunctor.normalizedFiberComparisons_exists {B : Type*} [Preorder B]
    (b₀ : B) (hb : ∀ b : B, b₀ ≤ b)
    (P : Pseudofunctor (LocallyDiscrete B) Cat.{d + 1, d + 2})
    {A : Type*} [Category A] (J : ∀ b : B, P.obj ⟨b⟩ ⥤ A)
    (a : ∀ {b c : B} (f : b ⟶ c), J b ≅ (P.map f.toLoc).toFunctor ⋙ J c)
    (h : ∀ b : B, Function.Bijective (fun u : J b ⟶ J b ↦
      whiskerLeft (P.map (homOfLE (hb b)).toLoc).toFunctor u)) :
    ∃! e : ∀ {b c : B} (f : b ⟶ c), J b ≅ (P.map f.toLoc).toFunctor ⋙ J c,
      (∀ (b : B) (X : P.obj ⟨b⟩),
        (e (𝟙 b)).hom.app X ≫ (J b).map ((P.mapId ⟨b⟩).hom.toNatTrans.app X) = 𝟙 _) ∧
      (∀ {b c d : B} (f : b ⟶ c) (g : c ⟶ d) (X : P.obj ⟨b⟩),
        (e (f ≫ g)).hom.app X ≫
            (J d).map ((P.mapComp f.toLoc g.toLoc).hom.toNatTrans.app X) =
          (e f).hom.app X ≫ (e g).hom.app ((P.map f.toLoc).toFunctor.obj X)) ∧
      (∀ {c d : B} (f : c ⟶ d),
        Functor.isoWhiskerLeft (P.map (homOfLE (hb c)).toLoc).toFunctor (e f) =
          (a (homOfLE (hb c))).symm ≪≫ a (homOfLE (hb d)) ≪≫
            Functor.isoWhiskerRight
              (Cat.Hom.toNatIso (P.mapComp (homOfLE (hb c)).toLoc f.toLoc)) (J d) ≪≫
                Functor.associator _ _ _)
